clue.text: Sliced duck in pleasant ambience failed to impress

parts.note: sliced means cut

indicators.note: the duck sits in what follows, so it goes inside the word for pleasant
an ambience is a surrounding atmosphere, so the pleasant word surrounds the duck

parts.note: pleasant means nice
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A diner's sliced duck, served in pleasant surroundings, somehow left them unimpressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is the cricket score of nought, not the bird. 'in' and 'ambience' together signal the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut no ice is an idiom for having no effect or making no impression on someone.

clue.text: Child's-play ward needing no special cleaning?

parts.note: child's play is something easy
ward means guardianship or protection, as in a child in care

explanation.surface: A children's hospital ward that never needs a deep clean.
explanation.walkthrough: Ward here is guardianship (as in 'watch and ward'), not a hospital room.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy-care fabrics or materials are those that can be washed simply, without special treatment.

clue.text: Cautiously dismissing student of Titian

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so the student's letter is dropped

parts.note: gingerly means cautiously
L, for learner, stands for a student

explanation.surface: Someone warily turning away a student of the painter Titian.
explanation.walkthrough: Titian is the painter, but titian is also an auburn hair colour named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian is a reddish-brown shade; something gingery has that orangey colouring.

clue.text: Late drinking gees up boozer ordering this?

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece swallows the other
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: late, meaning dead, is gone
gees are letters G, so two of them

explanation.surface: A late-night drinker urging the horses on, at a pub, ordering a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gees up' looks like urging horses on, but gees are two Gs, 'drinking' them while 'up' reads the word for late from the bottom, giving ENOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a festive drink of eggs, milk and spirits that a drinker might order.

clue.text: Type of acid trip curtailed in Islington clubs?

indicators.note: in places the shortened trip inside the other letters

parts.note: N1 is the London postcode of Islington, written as NI
C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: Is a drug trip cut short in North London nightclubs?
explanation.walkthrough: N1 is Islington's London postcode, read as NI. 'curtailed' cuts the trip, and 'in' places it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitric acid is a strong mineral acid, one particular kind of acid.

clue.text: Film made by English money perhaps Bergman mostly appreciated

parts.note: a ducat is an old gold coin, an example of money

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: Ingrid Bergman, the film actress
TA is slang for thank you, an appreciation

explanation.surface: A film produced with English funds that Ingrid Bergman mostly enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims INGRID to INGRI. TA is British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Educating Rita is a 1983 British film starring Michael Caine and Julie Walters.

clue.text: Artist drew frantically to capture central view

indicators.note: capturing means holding inside, so the jumbled letters enclose the rest
frantically suggests wild disorder, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
inland means away from the coast, central
to view is to see

explanation.surface: A painter sketching wildly to catch a view from the middle of things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantically' rearranges the letters of drew into EDWR, and 'to capture' puts the rest between its third and fourth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter famed for his animal pictures and Trafalgar Square's lions.

clue.text: Keep half of Duran Duran working on project in magazine

indicators.note: working suggests something reworked, so these letters are rearranged
half of means only the first half of the band's doubled name is used
in places one word inside the magazine's name

parts.note: Elle is a fashion magazine
to project is to cast or throw

explanation.surface: Duran Duran's members split, with one half working on a magazine project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps one copy of the band's doubled name, 'working' rearranges it, and 'in' signals the enclosure. Keep looks like a verb but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the main tower of a castle, so a whole castle can be a keep; Arundel Castle is in West Sussex.

clue.text: Normal seeing Mark sometime between eight and nine

definitions.meaning: 20/20 vision is normal sharpness of sight

definitions.text: Mark sometime between eight and nine
definitions.meaning: 20:20 on the 24-hour clock is ... past eight in the evening

explanation.surface: Someone with ordinary eyesight spotting Mark arriving after eight.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a man's name; it is a point marked on the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty-twenty is the standard measure of normal vision, and also the time 20:20.

clue.text: Big bank, sort of, attracting our other son

parts.note: a gene bank is a sort of bank

indicators.note: other suggests a different form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A big bank bringing in a second son of ours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' turns OUR into ROU. 'bank, sort of' is GENE, from gene bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Big in the sense of big-hearted: a generous person gives freely.

clue.text: He raced among cream in middle-distance?

definitions.text: He raced among cream in middle-distance?

indicators.note: in middle points to the central letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A runner competing among the elite at middle distances.
explanation.walkthrough: The centres of raced, among and cream give the answer; Sebastian Coe was among the cream of middle-distance runners.
explanation.definitionFit: Sebastian Coe won Olympic gold at 1500 metres, a middle-distance event.

clue.text: Cat with zero resistance being in pain

indicators.note: with ... in means the cat now has IN where zero and resistance were

parts.note: an Angora is a breed of long-haired cat
zero is the letter O
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A cat in pain, offering no resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: OR in ANGORA is swapped for IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is chest pain caused by poor blood supply to the heart.

clue.text: Something on plate that is cut by officers investigating butcher

parts.note: a British number plate shows a registration, shortened to reg

indicators.note: cut by means split open, so the officers go inside

parts.note: IE is the abbreviation for id est, that is
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, plain-clothes police officers

explanation.surface: Detectives investigating a butcher find a clue on a car plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut by' signals the enclosure. Chambers lists regicide as a person, the killer of a king, not only the act.
explanation.definitionFit: A regicide is one who kills a king, a royal slaughterer.

clue.text: Swimmer buoyant in Mediterranean

indicators.note: buoyant means floating upwards, in a down clue reading from the bottom
in means the letters are found inside the word

explanation.surface: A swimmer staying afloat easily in the salty Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds EDI inside Mediterranean, and 'buoyant' turns it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The ide is a freshwater fish of the carp family, so a swimmer.

clue.text: Describing lasagne, starter in eatery during repeated plonk

indicators.note: during means inside, so the starter falls within the two plonks

parts.note: plonk twice: to plonk is to lay down, and plonk is cheap red wine

indicators.note: starter in means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A food writer describes a restaurant's lasagne while drinking cheap wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Plonk does double duty: to put down, and cheap wine. 'during' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Lasagne is made in layers of pasta and sauce, so it is layered.

clue.text: Yearning for the other channel

definitions.meaning: an animal's sexual urge; 'the other' is British slang for sex

explanation.walkthrough: 'The other' is British euphemism for sex, not another channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Rut means a period of sexual excitement in deer and also a track worn into the ground.

clue.text: One leaves European port carrying large support for table?

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the port contains the letter
leaves means goes away, so the letter departs

parts.note: Trieste is an Italian port
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a European port carrying a large table support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' drops I from TRIESTE to give TRESTE, and 'carrying' puts L inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a frame of legs supporting a tabletop.

clue.text: Spinning pants used by a right-winger

parts.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, rot
a Tory is a British Conservative

explanation.surface: A right-wing politician wearing spinning underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants is British slang for nonsense, not underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotatory means turning round an axis, as something spinning does.

clue.text: Dick perhaps transported fencing gear to compound

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the outer word surrounds the jumbled one

parts.note: transported means sent

indicators.note: to compound is to mix up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective delivers fencing equipment to a prison compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to compound' rearranges the letters of gear, and 'fencing' encloses them. Dick is old slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick is slang for a detective; a detective sergeant is one such officer.

clue.text: Pianist shortly brought in performed on triangle

indicators.note: brought in means placed inside

parts.note: performed means did

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: Elton John, pianist and singer

explanation.surface: A pianist is hastily brought in to play the triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: The pianist is Elton John; 'shortly' drops his last letter and 'brought in' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A deltoid is a kite-shaped figure, named from the triangular Greek delta.

clue.text: Gurner maybe heading for Egremont, Cumbrian place at heart of event

indicators.note: heading for points to the first letter of the town

parts.note: Dent is a village in Cumbria

indicators.note: heart of points to the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A gurning contestant heading for Egremont, the Cumbrian village hosting the event.
explanation.walkthrough: Egremont, Cumbria, hosts the World Gurning Championship, face-pulling often done by the toothless.
explanation.definitionFit: Edentate means toothless, and gurners often pull faces with no teeth in.

clue.text: Refusal to move loaf above freezer

indicators.note: above in a down clue puts the first piece on top of the second

parts.note: loaf is head (from loaf of bread, rhyming slang), and to nod is to move it
ice is a freezer

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to move a loaf of bread from on top of the freezer.
explanation.walkthrough: Loaf is Cockney rhyming slang for head (loaf of bread).
explanation.definitionFit: No dice is an informal phrase for a refusal or no luck.

clue.text: Antique George left in trailer

indicators.note: in places the pieces inside the advertisement

parts.note: a trailer advertises a film, an ad

explanation.surface: An antique left by George in a trailer.
explanation.walkthrough: Trailer is a film advert, not a towed vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Antique as an adjective means very old, as does age-old.

clue.text: Sauce spilling on new fabric

indicators.note: spilling means losing, so these letters are dropped

parts.note: tartare is a mayonnaise sauce
on means about, re

explanation.surface: Sauce spilt over a new piece of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilling' drops RE from TARTARE, giving TARTA.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartan is a woollen cloth woven in checks, a fabric.

clue.text: Board over many a school — is it common?

definitions.meaning: an ..., Local Education Authority, runs many British schools
open grassland, like a village common

explanation.surface: A governing board asks whether something is common to many schools.
explanation.walkthrough: A common is a public patch of grass; lea is a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Lea is an old word for a meadow, and LEA a British education authority.

clue.text: Passed on official document that tipster recommends?

parts.note: passed on means died, dead
cert is short for certificate, an official document

explanation.surface: A death certificate that a racing tipster recommends.
explanation.walkthrough: Passed on and official document suggest a death certificate.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead cert is a racing bet certain to win, which a tipster would recommend.

clue.text: See 8
Being awkward on tour, Alice Cooper abandoned musical style

indicators.note: on tour means travelling about, so these letters are moved around

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: abandoned means emptied, so only the outer letters of the surname stay

parts.note: trance is a style of electronic dance music

explanation.surface: Alice Cooper, difficult on tour, drops a musical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' empties COOPER to CR, and 'on tour' turns ALICECR into RECALCI.
explanation.definitionFit: Recalcitrance is obstinate unwillingness to cooperate, being difficult.
